title: How to Negotiate Salary: Understanding Casual Loading and Super Paid on Top
description: Learn how to negotiate salary with confidence using our hourly to annual conversion guide. Includes casual loading, super, and tax estimates for 2026-27.
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week, your annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours times 52 weeks, with casual loading and super added on top.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role of 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your annual gross pay before tax and super. If you are casual, add 25% casual loading to your base rate before multiplying.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the minimum hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave entitlements like annual leave or sick leave. For example, if the base rate is $26.44 per hour, a casual employee receives $33.05 per hour. This loading is included in your hourly rate before calculating annual pay.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on top of my salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings at a rate of 12% (from 1 July 2026). It is not deducted from your salary. The super guarantee applies up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, if your annual ordinary earnings are $50,000, your employer contributes an additional $6,000 to your super fund.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Negotiate Salary: Know Your Worth

When you're looking at a job offer or thinking about a pay rise, understanding how your hourly rate translates into annual earnings is essential. Knowing the numbers helps you **how to negotiate salary** with confidence. This guide explains the conversion, the role of casual loading, and how superannuation is paid on top.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly to Annual

The standard way to estimate your annual gross pay is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For a full-time employee working 38 ordinary hours per week (the standard under most awards), the calculation becomes:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, if your hourly rate is $30.00:
- Weekly pay: $30.00 × 38 = $1,140.00
- Fortnightly pay: $1,140.00 × 2 = $2,280.00
- Annual gross: $1,140.00 × 52 = $59,280.00

This assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to run your own numbers.

### The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage (NMW) is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Commission. This is the minimum for award/agreement-free employees aged 21 and over. However, most workers are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides for each award, including penalty rates and allowances.

If you are covered by an award, your minimum rate will be higher than the NMW. For example, the Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services Industry Award (SCHADS) has specific rates that may include additional increases from 1 December 2026.

### Casual Loading: An Extra 25%

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. This loading is included in the hourly rate you see on your payslip. For the NMW, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25).

When calculating your annual pay as a casual, use the loaded rate in the formula. For example, if your casual rate is $33.05:
- Weekly: $33.05 × 38 = $1,255.90
- Fortnightly: $2,511.80
- Annual: $65,306.80

Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains more about how this works.

### Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Superannuation is not deducted from your salary; it is an additional contribution your employer makes to your super fund. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, if your annual ordinary earnings are $60,000, your employer adds $7,200 to your super.

This means your total remuneration package includes your salary plus super. When comparing job offers, consider the total package, not just the base salary.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) applies progressive tax rates for 2026–27:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds are not yet confirmed). Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator to estimate your net income.

### How to Negotiate Salary Using These Figures

Armed with the conversion formula and knowledge of casual loading and super, you can approach salary negotiations with data. Here are a few tips:

- **Know the award rate**: Check the relevant pay guide from the Fair Work Ombudsman to ensure the offer meets minimum standards.
- **Factor in super**: Remember that super is on top. If an employer offers $70,000 plus super, your total package is $78,400.
- **Compare total remuneration**: When negotiating, talk about the total package including super, not just the base salary.
- **Use the fortnightly figure**: Some employers think in fortnightly pay cycles. Knowing your fortnightly equivalent can help in discussions.

### Important Disclaimer

This guide provides estimates only. Annual pay is calculated as hourly rate × hours per week × 52, assuming the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For personalised calculations, refer to the [reference tables](/data) on our site or consult a qualified accountant.
